neighbours.label: 'of' (or the article) right after a 'totality / sum' head in a definitional gloss ('X is the totality of ...')
fire: Public opinion is the totality of views held by the people of a country.
A person's character is the sum total of their habits and choices.
By folklore we mean the totality of tales, customs and sayings of a people.
National income is the aggregate of all wages, rents and profits earned in a year.
An ecosystem is the totality of living things and their physical setting.
The canon is the whole body of works accepted as genuine.
A language's lexicon is the totality of its words and fixed phrases.
Experience is the sum of everything a person has lived through.
quiet: Public opinion shifted sharply after the debate on television.
Small daily habits and choices reveal a person's character.
Folklore collectors recorded tales, customs and sayings in the villages.
National income fell for the third year in a row.
After a forest fire an ecosystem can recover slowly.
Scholars fixed the canon in the fourth century.
A cup of flour and a pinch of salt go into the bowl.
The price of bread rose again in the spring.
